result.text: You crossed the falls and reached the sea; the survey hut at Vell Foot is still standing, door shut, kettle on the shelf. Tomas Lind's 1983 notice mixes up the tea and nail tins, then offers shelter to a walker caught in bad weather. A later, unsigned note says its writer went to look for the stakes, could not find them, and left the tea. It is pinned to the hut door; I have left it there. In his field notebook, Tomas re-drilled stake four and measured the ice front twice because he did not like the number. The bolted stone is intact; its bolt is stamped VELL 1979. I set the register beside this page.

Distinguish the notes.

“The man who kept the stake line had less use for jokes” is unsupported and sits uneasily with his joking note about not moving the boulder. Keep to what the records show: he re-drilled stake four and measured the ice front twice because he did not like the number.
